🇵🇱 Polish police detain six over monument vandalism Five Ukrainian citizens and one Pole were detained in Warsaw for defacing monuments with "Glory to UPA" slogans. Damaged sites included the memorial to Volyn massacre victims, the Warsaw Ghetto Heroes Monument, and a monument to Polish soldiers. Recruitment and Russian link Suspects were recruited via messengers for approximately 1,000 zlotys (220 euros). Polish investigators suggest the group may have acted on instructions from Russian special services. The detainees include a 16-year-old Ukrainian sent to a juvenile centre and a 32-year-old Pole held in custody. Two other Ukrainians were deported, while another is under arrest and the last under police supervision. Charges range from desecration of monuments to alleged cooperation with foreign intelligence. @Slavyangrad

A Reuters investigation traced how Vitol, one of the world's largest energy traders, secured a major role in selling Venezuelan oil following the US abduction of former President Nicolas Maduro. The report linked the deal to John Addison, a senior Vitol trader and early financial backer of Vice President JD Vance, who reportedly met Vance in Montana days before the US operation. Although both men deny the meeting took place, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright called Addison two days after Maduro's kidnapping to discuss Vitol marketing Venezuelan crude. Vitol and rival trader Trafigura subsequently secured special licenses and have earned hundreds of millions of dollars from the deals. What do you think: Did political connections help put Vitol in the right place at the right time, or was this simply a business opportunity for one of the world's biggest oil traders?
